Rashi on Temurah 14b:13:1.english: So too, libations [are offered] during the day:

Rashi on Temurah 14b:13:2.hebrew: לרבות שלמי נזיר - דאי שלמי נדבה, הרי כבר אמור "נדבותיכם". ואי משום הקישא, לכתוב "ולשלמים":
Rashi on Temurah 14b:13:2.english: To include the peace offerings of a nazirite - For if [it meant] voluntary peace offerings, behold it has already been stated "your voluntary offerings." And if [it were needed] because of the juxtaposition, [the verse] should have written "and the peace offerings" [without the suffix "your"].

Rashi on Temurah 14b:14:1.hebrew: שלמי פסח - חגיגת י"ד, שכשהיתה חבורה מרובה נמנים על הפסח ואינו סיפק להן, היו מביאין עמו שלמים. ואם הפרישן לשם כך ולא הקריבום, יקריבום בחוה"מ. דאי שלמי נזיר, לא צריכי ריבוי לרבויי, דמנדריכם ונדבותיכם נפקא, דנזירות ע"י נדר בא עליו, ונידר ונידב קרינא ביה. אבל שלמי פסח חובה נינהו, כדמפרש בפסחים בפ' ואלו דברים (דף עא.):
Rashi on Temurah 14b:14:1.english: The peace offerings of the Paschal offering - The festival offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan]: when a large group was counted together for a Paschal offering and it was not enough for them, they would bring peace offerings along with it. And if one set them aside for this purpose and did not sacrifice them, he sacrifices them during the intermediate days of the Festival. For if [the verse meant] the peace offerings of a nazirite, there would be no need for an inclusion to include them, since they are derived from "your vows and your voluntary offerings," as nazirite status comes upon a person through a vow, and we call it "vowed and contributed." But Paschal peace offerings are obligatory, as [the Gemara] explains in Pesachim, in the chapter [entitled] "These are the things" (page 71a).

Rashi on Temurah 14b:16:1.hebrew: והנזירות קרב בבמת יחיד - אלמא נידר ונידב חשיב ליה, דאי לאו הכי לא הוה קרב בבמת יחיד:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:16:1.english: And the offerings of a nazirite are sacrificed on a private altar - Evidently, [Rabbi Meir] considers it [the nazirite's offering] to be among the offerings that are vowed or contributed voluntarily; for if it were not so, it would not be sacrificed on a private altar.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:16:2.hebrew: סמי מכאן נזירות - דאע"ג דנזירות באה עליו ע"י נדר, אין הקרבנות נקראין נידר ונידב. דהא לא נדר אלא מן היין, והקרבן מאיליו מוטל עליו חובה:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:16:2.english: Delete from here [the case of] a nazirite - For although the nazirite status comes upon him by means of a vow, the offerings are not called “vowed” or “donated.” For he vowed only [to abstain] from wine, and the offering is imposed upon him of its own accord as an obligation.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:17:1.hebrew: אשר נדרתי לה' בחברון - משמע: בחברון אלך, ואשלמה שם נדרי. וההוא נדר נזירות היה, דאבשלום נזיר עולם היה, ומשלשים לשלשים יום היה מגלח ומביא קרבן. ומדהלך להקריב קרבנות נזירותיו בחברון, דהיא במת יחיד, שמע מינה נידר ונידב הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:17:1.english: “Which I vowed to the Lord in Hebron” - This implies: “I will go to Hebron and fulfill my vow there.” And that vow was a nazirite vow, for Absalom was a lifelong nazirite, and every thirty days he would shave and bring an offering. Since he went to offer his nazirite offerings in Hebron, which was a private altar, conclude from this that [the nazirite offering] is vowed and donated voluntarily.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:18:1.hebrew: אעיקר נדרו קאי - האי בחברון, וה"ק אלכה נא לבמה גדולה בגבעון — דהתם הוא מזבח שעשה משה — ואשלמה נדרי שנדרתי בחברון, אבל לא שיביא הקרבן בחברון:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:18:1.english: It refers to his principal vow - This "in Hebron" [refers to the principal vow]. And this is what [Absalom] meant: "Let me go to the great high place at Gibeon," for there was the altar that Moses made, "and I will fulfill my vows that I vowed in Hebron," but not that he would bring the offering in Hebron.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:18:2.hebrew: והא בגשור כו' - דכתיב: כי נדר נדר עבדך בשבתי בגשור וגו':
Rashi on Temurah 14b:18:2.english: But [was it not] in Geshur, etc. - For it is written: "For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelled at Geshur," etc.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:19:1.hebrew: להביא כבשים - ולהקריבן שוב בבמה גדולה. וה"ק: אשלמה את נדרי, כלומר, אשלמה את נזירותי ואגלח, ומחברון אביא הכבשים. ולהכי פריך בגמרא: מחברון מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:19:1.english: To bring sheep - and to offer them afterward on the great high place. And this is what [the verse] is saying: "Let me pay my vow," meaning, let me complete my nazirite vow and shave [my hair], and from Hebron I will bring the sheep. And for this reason [the Gemara] objects: [The verse] should have said "from Hebron."

Rashi on Temurah 14b:19:2.hebrew: בחברון - היו בו כבשים שמנים, כמו שבמס' מנחות (דף פז.):
Rashi on Temurah 14b:19:2.english: In Hebron - There were fat sheep there, as [stated] in tractate Menachot (87a).

Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:1.hebrew: לא תיסמי נסכים - מההיא מתני' דלעיל, ומצי לתרוצי:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:1.english: He should not delete "the libations" - the word from that Mishnah above, and he is able to resolve the contradiction in the other way.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:2.hebrew: הא - דקתני נסכים בהדי דברים שדרכן ליקרב ביום, היינו בנסכים הבאין עם הזבח:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:2.english: This - That which it teaches [the laws of] libations together with things whose manner is to be sacrificed by day, that is, [it refers] to libations that come with the animal offering.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:3.hebrew: בפני עצמן - שלא קדשו בשחיטת הזבח, יכול להקריב בלילה:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:1:3.english: By themselves - [Libations] that were not sanctified through the slaughter of the animal offering; one can sacrifice [them] at night.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:21:1.hebrew: אלא לעולם לאקרובי - הלך אבשלום לחברון דנזירות בבמת יחיד:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:21:1.english: Rather, actually, to sacrifice - [Absalom went to Hebron] to sacrifice the offerings of his naziriteship on a private altar.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:21:2.hebrew: תיקשי לך גבעון - דשם היה מזבח שעשה משה:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:21:2.english: Let Gibeon pose a difficulty for you - For there [was] the altar that Moses made:

Rashi on Temurah 14b:2:1.hebrew: כשורפי התורה - שאין מצילין אותן בשבת בפני הדליקה. ל"א, שאסור להשהותן כתובים, דתורה שבעל פה היא:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:2:1.english: Like those who burn the Torah - For one does not rescue them on Shabbat from a fire. Another explanation: It is forbidden to keep them in written form, for it is the Oral Torah.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:2:2.english: And one who learns from them - From the books:

Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:1.hebrew: חדתא - חדשה, שהיא מילתא שלא היו יודעין לתרץ את הברייתות:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:1.english: A new [matter] - A new [matter], that they did not know how to resolve the baraitot.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:2.hebrew: [ל"א] חדתי - פירושו לחדש דבר, כגון זו שחדשה היא:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:2.english: [Another version:] Ḥadati - It means to innovate a matter, such as this one, which is new:

Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:3.hebrew: מעייני בספר אגדתא - היו מעיינים שלא ישתכחו:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:3.english: They would read from a scroll of aggada - [They would study it] so that [its teachings] would not be forgotten.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:4.hebrew: עת לעשות לה' - כשעושין הדבר לשם קדושת השם, ראוי להפר תורתך, ומוטב תעקר כו':
Rashi on Temurah 14b:5:4.english: It is time to act for the Lord - When one does the thing for the sake of sanctifying the Name, it is proper to "make void Your Torah," and it is better that [one law of the Torah] be uprooted, etc.:

Rashi on Temurah 14b:6:1.hebrew: השתא דאמרת כו' - יכול אדם להקדישן ולהקריבן בלילה אחת. ל"א גרסינן: עלות השחר פוסל בהן כאברים. כלומר, הא דאמרינן נזדמנו לו נסכים בלילה, מקדישן בלילה [ומקריבן]:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:6:1.english: Now that you have said, etc. - [A person] can consecrate them and sacrifice them in the same night. Another version: We read, "The break of dawn disqualifies them, like [sacrificial] limbs." That is to say, this [statement] that we said — if libations came to hand at night, one consecrates them at night [and sacrifices them].

Rashi on Temurah 14b:8:1.hebrew: כאברים - כמו האיברים של תמיד, במס' זבחים (פז.). וכן עיקר הגהת הרב:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:8:1.english: Like limbs - Like the limbs of the daily offering, in tractate Zevachim (87a). And so is the essential emendation of the Rav.

Rashi on Temurah 14b:9:1.hebrew: חובות הבאות מחמת הרגל ברגל - כגון עולת ראיה, וחגיגה, ומוספין:
Rashi on Temurah 14b:9:1.english: Obligations that come because of the Festival, on the Festival - For example, the burnt offering of appearance, the Festival offering, and the additional offerings.

Tosafot on Temurah 14b:16:1.hebrew: ותנן המנחות והנזירות בבמת יחיד דברי ר' מאיר - הוה מצי לשנויי: תנאי היא, שהרי בפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיז.) פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי מאיר, ומסיק התם דמנחות ונזירות איכא בינייהו:
Tosafot on Temurah 14b:16:1.english: "And we learned: The meal offerings and the offerings of a nazirite [are sacrificed] on a private altar; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir" - [The Gemara] could have answered: It is a dispute between Tannaim, for in the last chapter of Zevachim (117a) the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Meir, and it concludes there that [the case of] meal offerings and offerings of a nazirite is [the point] on which they differ:

Tosafot on Temurah 14b:16:2.hebrew: סמי מכאן נזירות - וה"ה דצריך כמו כן למיסמייה מההיא דפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיז: ע"ש), דאמר: מנחות ונזירות איכא בינייהו:
Tosafot on Temurah 14b:16:2.english: Delete "nazirite" from here - And the same applies: one likewise needs to delete it from that passage in the last chapter of Zevachim (117b, see there), which says: "Meal offerings and nazirite offerings are the point of difference between them."

Tosafot on Temurah 14b:3:1.hebrew: דברים שבכתב אי אתה רשאי לאומרם בעל פה - וא"ת: היכי קאמרינן מזמורים על פה? וי"ל: דאין להקפיד רק מה שכתוב בחומש. אמנם קשה: היכי קרינן ויושע וקריאת שמע? וי"ל: דאין להקפיד אלא בדבר שמוציא אחרים ידי חובתן:
Tosafot on Temurah 14b:3:1.english: "Words that are written, you may not recite them orally" - And if you ask: How do we recite Psalms by heart? And one can answer: One need only be careful about what is written in the Pentateuch. However, it is difficult: How do we recite Vayosha [the Song at the Sea] and the Shema [by heart]? And one can answer: One need only be careful regarding something by which one fulfills the obligation of others [who are listening]:
